description: We're a team of tech enthusiasts passionate about space exploration, game development, and making learning fun. We're building LunaQuest, an interactive lunar base management game where kids take on the role of junior astronauts, managing resources like food, water, and energy while discovering fascinating facts about space. We're looking for creative minds with skills in game development, UI/UX design, 3D modeling, science, and storytelling to join our mission!

details:
What we built and how it works

LunaQuest: Survival Mission is a browser-based educational game created by Team Tantaropic for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.” It helps children ages 7–12 explore the decisions involved in keeping a fictional lunar outpost alive.

Players balance food, water, oxygen and energy across five facilities: the Habitat, Greenhouse, Solar Array, Shelter and Landing Pad. They grow crops, recycle oxygen, repair equipment, collect Earth supplies and respond to scripted solar storms and an oxygen leak. Each action has a resource cost, so players must plan ahead.

Chicken Hunt connects arcade entertainment with this survival loop. Players spend six energy to launch a 35-second fictional supply mission, dodge alien birds and collect food. A safe return adds cargo to the base’s shared resources; destruction forfeits it. Seven short learning guides explain each system through “What?”, “Why?” and “Your Mission.”

Benefits and intended impact

LunaQuest is designed to make space-system trade-offs understandable and enjoyable. Players can practice preparation, prioritization and recovery from mistakes rather than only memorizing facts. Our intended impact is to encourage STEM curiosity and support future classroom learning; educational outcomes have not yet been measured.

Tools and development

We used Phaser, TypeScript, React and Vite to build the game, GitHub for source management, Vercel for hosting, and Vitest and Playwright for testing tools. The reviewed build passed 156 unit tests and its production build.

Codex and Antigravity assisted with coding and implementation. Our team originated the idea, designed the architecture, ran tests and debugged the solution. No specialized hardware is required to play.

Creativity and design considerations

Our creative approach combines a connected urvival economy, arcade supply missions and learning at the moment of action. NASA DONKI observations provide real solar-activity context, with a clearly labeled historical fallback. They do not control game emergencies or predict lunar radiation exposure.

We considered age-appropriate language, keyboard and touch controls, browser-local saves, adjustable audio, clear resource feedback and reliable play when NASA data is unavailable. Scientific accuracy and transparency guided us: game values are illustrative, arcade combat is fictional, and long-term resource balance remains a prototype limitation.
